hypothesis: No candidate family among {LogReg-L2, LogReg-L1, RandomForest, ExtraTrees, HistGradientBoosting, LightGBM} is assumed superior a priori; measure all six under the same protocol/features/folds.
baseline: none (first family-wide comparison of these six)
single_change: model family only; features/folds/preprocessing/seed held fixed
statistical_comparison: paired t-test, Holm-Bonferroni over 15 pairwise comparisons
decision: KEEP: RandomForest/HistGradientBoosting/LightGBM mutually INDISTINGUISHABLE (all underpowered, diffs 0.009-0.019 << MDE 0.164) and each decisively beats LogReg-L1/L2 and ExtraTrees (p_holm<0.03). REJECT ExtraTrees and both LogReg variants as the sole production candidate family. INCONCLUSIVE on which of {RF,HGB,LightGBM} is best - data cannot resolve it.
interpretation: Best-split search (RF/HGB/LightGBM) matters far more than ensemble mechanism (bagging vs boosting) or added expressiveness; ExtraTrees (random-split) underperforms RF by 0.262 nAP (p_holm=0.008) despite identical depth/leaf hyperparameters, isolating split-selection as the likely mechanism (imbalanced, skewed-amount features punish random thresholds). This reframes Phase 6: the open question is NOT which best-split tree ensemble to ship, but whether features/representation/labels are the binding constraint on further gains.
runtime_note: LogisticRegression_L1 (liblinear solver) took 679.7s vs <12s for every tree method on the same 208k-row x 24-feature x 12-fold job - a 60-170x runtime cost for a statistically indistinguishable-from-L2 result. Recorded as a lesson: do not default to liblinear L1 at this data scale in later experiments.

hypothesis: Given exp01 (RF/HGB/LightGBM statistically tied), the bottleneck question is which feature GROUP carries ranking signal, not which tree ensemble. Leave-one-group-out and single-group-only ablation over Groups A/B/C/D (Group E absent from this dataset) isolates each group's contribution.
single_change: feature set only; model=LightGBM fixed, folds/seed/preprocessing fixed
statistical_comparison: paired t-test, Holm-Bonferroni across full ablation family

hypothesis: Single-fold diagnostic (largest-history/worst-case fold t<=38->t39-40) to characterize false negatives/positives beyond aggregate nAP.
decision: FINDING: false negatives are disproportionately cold-start addresses (median n_txs_asof_t=0 for 511 FNs vs median=1 for true positives at K=100). Connects to exp02: Group B (history) is a real contributor and its absence for cold-start addresses is the likely mechanism. Flags counterparty-side history as the clearest untested feature-engineering lead.

hypothesis: Isotonic calibration collapses score resolution on PS-native v2 (reproducing the Phase-6-scope finding on this scope specifically) and this has a measurable, tie-bound effect on precision@K at investigator-realistic budgets.
baseline: raw LightGBM score, same fold as exp03
single_change: raw score vs isotonic-calibrated score (calibrator fit on held-out 15pct of fold training data)
statistical_comparison: none - single fold, tie-bound widths reported directly
decision: CONFIRMED (new measurement): isotonic tie-collapse causes precision@50 bound width of 0.26 (0.16-0.42) vs 0.02 for raw score. INCONCLUSIVE on Brier direction (this fold regressed, contradicting v1 artifacts improvement) - flagged as anomaly, not resolved. Supports rank-on-raw-score / calibrated-as-display-only policy already proposed in HANDOFF.md.

hypothesis: ps_model.py current explanation method (global feature_importances_ x |value|, direction from whether overall calibrated_p>=0.5) diverges materially from true per-prediction TreeSHAP attributions on the same fitted model.
baseline: exact TreeSHAP via LightGBM booster.predict(pred_contrib=True) (verified locally exact: reconstruction error 1.91e-14)
single_change: explanation method only; same model, same rows, same fold as exp03/exp04
statistical_comparison: none - descriptive, but n=1500 (feature,row) pairs is large enough that 33.9% vs 50% chance agreement is not sampling noise
decision: REJECT the current explanation method as faithful: top-3 feature overlap with true TreeSHAP is only 1.4/3 on average (9% totally disjoint); direction label agrees with the true per-feature SHAP sign only 33.9% of the time - WORSE than a coin flip, because direction is derived from the overall prediction crossing 0.5, not from the feature. This is the single most operationally serious finding in the program: investigator-facing explanations are directionally wrong more often than right.

hypothesis: Given exp01's tied tree tier {RF,HGB,LightGBM} and rejected {ExtraTrees,LogReg}, do justified variants (class-weighting, capacity, a native ranking objective, more ExtraTrees estimators) produce a defensible improvement over the tied tier, compared without re-running exp01's original candidates?
baseline: exp01 LightGBM/RandomForest/HistGradientBoosting/ExtraTrees (reconstructed from saved per-fold results, not refit)
statistical_comparison: paired t-test, Holm-Bonferroni across full (reconstructed+new) family
decision: INCONCLUSIVE/REJECT, no improvement found: all 6 new variants (LightGBM_balanced, LightGBM_deeper, LightGBM_lambdarank(chunked), RandomForest_balanced, HistGradientBoosting_balanced) are statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE from the exp01 tied tier across all 45 pairwise comparisons in the corrected family (every comparison either not significant after Holm correction or below MDE 0.164, mostly both). Class-weighted variants are numerically worse than their unweighted counterparts in all 3 cases tested (descriptive pattern only, not statistically decisive). LightGBM_deeper (3x estimators, more leaves, lower LR) does not improve on plain LightGBM (diff 0.019, indistinguishable) - confirms model capacity is not the bottleneck, consistent with 06_ablation_results.md. LightGBM_lambdarank (necessarily chunked into ~9000-row groups due to a hard LightGBM per-query row limit) numerically underperforms plain LightGBM, not statistically decisive given the large corrected family - a genuine, informative negative result for this specific engineering compromise, not evidence against ranking objectives in general. ExtraTrees_500trees CLOSES the previously flagged open question from 05_model_comparison.md: REJECT the hypothesis that more estimators closes the ExtraTrees-vs-RandomForest gap (0.3034 vs 0.3103 at 100 trees, indistinguishable, both far below RandomForest 0.5723) - confirms the gap is a split-selection-quality mechanism, not an under-averaging one. XGBoost: NOT_TESTED, ModuleNotFoundError, not vendored offline.

hypothesis: 13_red_team_review.md flagged exp02's Group-A-dominant / Group-C,D-weak finding as measured on LightGBM only. Repeat the same leave-one-group-out design on RandomForest to check whether the finding is data-driven or a LightGBM-specific artefact.
single_change: model=RandomForest instead of LightGBM; features/folds/seed fixed
statistical_comparison: paired t-test, Holm-Bonferroni across ablation family
decision: CONFIRMED, generalizes beyond LightGBM: on RandomForest, minus_A collapses nAP 0.572->0.274 (p_holm=0.001, even more decisive than on LightGBM). minus_B is small/borderline (p_holm=0.156, not significant after correction - slightly weaker than LightGBMs borderline-significant 0.048 but same qualitative story). minus_C not significant (p_holm=0.156, matches LightGBMs 0.126). minus_D changes essentially nothing (p=0.941, matches LightGBMs 0.653 almost exactly). Closes the scope limitation flagged in 13_red_team_review.md: Group A dominance and Group C/D weakness are DATA-DRIVEN findings, not LightGBM-specific artefacts.

hypothesis: Counterparty-side transaction history (does THIS transaction touch another address with its own track record?) recovers ranking quality specifically on cold-start addresses (07_error_analysis.md's dominant false-negative population), even though the subject address itself has no history.
dataset_version: ps_native_features/2 + new experimental columns (reproduced from raw Elliptic++ files, verified against real train/validation.parquet)
feature_version: CORE + counterparty (experimental, not in production pipeline/features_ps.py)
decision: INCONCLUSIVE (promising, not yet confirmed): CORE+counterparty nAP 0.6155 vs baseline 0.5914 (diff +0.0241), consistent DIRECTION on both the full 12-fold family test and the cold-start subset specifically (0.2464 vs 0.2387), but the full-family comparison is INDISTINGUISHABLE (p=0.199, well below MDE 0.164 - underpowered to confirm at this magnitude with a 2-candidate, 12-fold design). Both new columns survived the feature-health check (not constant/duplicate). Dataset reconstruction independently verified to match the real train/validation.parquet address+txid sets exactly before trusting any result. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to 07_error_analysis.md: 90.9% of ALL rows in the diagnostic fold eval set are cold-start (n_txs_asof_t==0), not a rare subpopulation - the original false-negative finding needs to be read against this base rate (see 07_error_analysis.md addendum). NEEDS_MORE_DATA: a larger or more sensitive counterparty feature set (diversity, not just max/mean prior count) or a properly-powered follow-up before promoting this feature to production.

hypothesis: A severity-band procedure that selects thresholds on a genuinely held-out split (never used for fitting or for the final reported precision) will show a smaller in-sample-to-generalization gap than reproducing the flawed same-sample procedure identified in 09_alert_policy_analysis.md.
baseline: v1 frozen calibration.json bands (thresholds and reported precision from the same sample)
single_change: threshold-selection split: corrected (separate) vs flawed (same-sample) procedure, same model/fold
model_version: LightGBM, exp01 hyperparameters, fit on 70pct of fold training data
decision: CORRECTED PROCEDURE VALIDATED for same-distribution generalization: thresholds picked on threshold_set (28608 rows, held out from fitting) generalize almost perfectly to holdout_check_set (another same-period held-out split): 0.900->0.902, 0.750->0.753, 0.500->0.494. This confirms the same-sample-threshold-selection bug identified in 09_alert_policy_analysis.md is fixable by proper splitting. HOWEVER, a DEEPER, more consequential problem surfaced: applying those SAME correctly-derived thresholds to the actual out-of-time fold eval window (a genuinely different period) still collapses precision (0.900->0.593, 0.750->0.482, 0.500->0.177) - i.e. the core defect is not merely same-sample tuning, it is TEMPORAL drift: static value thresholds do not survive a new time window regardless of how carefully they were derived. This reinforces ml/protocol.pys own central thesis (window variance dominates) applied specifically to alert thresholds. Secondary check (reproducing the flawed same-sample procedure on this specific worst-case fold) gave a confusing, non-illustrative result (thresholds derived in-sample on this unusually hard fold happened to transfer ACCEPTABLY to the training-period holdout for HIGH/MEDIUM, and CRITICAL was unreachable at all on this fold) - flagged honestly as fold-specific noise, not forced into the original narrative.

decision: CONFIRMED: production features_ps.py Group E code is a stub - observer_diversity/peer_count hardcoded to 1.0 regardless of real underlying variation (verified: real data has peer_count range 1-8, mean 5.67). NOT tautological at single-feature level (AUC 0.745-0.755, not 0.95+). hypothesis: On the synthetic world (the only dataset in this program where chain and network structure share a real generative cause), does a PROPERLY aggregated Group E network feature set add value over Groups A-D, and does it differ from the current production STUB implementation (confirmed constant in exp11)?
baseline: CORE_only (Groups A-D, unmodified production feature engine)
single_change: network feature variant: none / properly-aggregated / production-stub
feature_version: CORE + Group E variants (research-only aggregation for the 'correct' variant)
model_version: RandomForest (200 trees, depth 5, leaf 3) - scaled down for ~900-row dataset
evaluation_protocol: standard rolling_origin_folds(), only 3 of 12 usable at this data volume
statistical_comparison: descriptive only - too few folds for compare_family's Holm/permutation machinery
decision: DECISIVE, UNEXPECTED FINDING (investigated as anomaly before trusting): nAP=1.0000 (exact, sd=0.0000) in ALL 3 usable folds for ALL THREE feature variants (CORE-only, CORE+correct-network, CORE+stub-network) - the task is fully saturated by Groups A-D alone, leaving no room for Group E (or anything else) to show incremental value. Confirmed via quarantined world_truth scenario labels (post-hoc diagnostic only, never fed to model): even MERCHANT_SWEEP, the generators own stated hardest adversarial case, separates from true positives by a ~7x score margin in every fold. Mechanistic explanation: deterministic, fixed-parameter behavior shapes (exact mixing_denomination=0.1, tight UNIFORM_SPREAD=0.02) leave no ambiguity for existing shape detectors to fail on. REJECT this world instance as a Group F/G benchmark as currently configured - ceiling effect, independent of and compounding the exp11 fold-count limitation. See 16_synthetic_world_investigation.md for the full reasoning and a scoped specification for what a genuinely useful next-generation instance would require.
